items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: Willie's, he was my oldest brother... I played the first brass band I played was for the Jefferson Buzzard, it was on the Carmel Day, with Willie Parker.

ctx.x: And I just wondered how long he'd known you and all that.

Oh, Willie, Willie would have been known before I was born. Willie's, he was my oldest brother. How old is your oldest brother? My oldest brother, he's beautiful, Willie Parker, he's around his 80s or something odd. He's my oldest brother. Then I had two brothers of size, you understand, he was older than me.
Were they, say, 15 years or 20 years older than you or what? My brothers? Yes, how much older were they?

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: Yeah, that's where St. Sophie is from.

ctx.x: I was wondering because that's where Willie Parker is from.
Yeah, that's where St. Sophie is from.
And I just wondered how long he'd known you and all that.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-06-15
items.q: That was the first parade I played too. Budapetit. With old man Parker, Willie Parker.

ctx.x: What ones? What was your first brass band you ever played with? I'll put it that way.

The first brass band I played with. See the New Orleans? That was on the carnival day, Budapetit. Budapetit on the carnival day. And that was the first parade I played too. Budapetit. With old man Parker, Willie Parker.
